title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第22部分：几何

chapters.Frontier: 15. 前沿：精确性、3SUM 与最近邻
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

08c9ad9af07e.en: Here is the most basic question in computational geometry. Is the point p to the left of the line through q and r, or to the right, or on it? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take q at twelve, twelve and r at twenty-four, twenty-four, and put p a whisker from the point one half, one half, a few floating-point steps off the line. <bookmark mark='b'/> The test is a two by two determinant, and the answer should not depend on which point we list first. In double precision it does. Ask it one way and p is on the left. Rotate the three points and p is exactly on the line. Rotate again and p is on the right. <bookmark mark='c'/> The true answer is right, every time. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is not a rare accident: near this line, thousands of the nearest floating-point points get contradictory answers, and algorithms built on contradictory answers crash, loop forever, or return hulls that are not convex.
08c9ad9af07e.zh: 这是计算几何中最基本的问题。点 p 在过 q 和 r 的直线的左边、右边，还是在线上？<bookmark mark='a'/>取 q 为十二、十二，r 为二十四、二十四，把 p 放在离点二分之一、二分之一极近的地方，离直线只差几个浮点数步长。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个测试是一个二乘二行列式，答案不应取决于先列出哪个点。在双精度下它却取决于此。这样问，p 在左边；把三个点轮换一下，p 恰好在线上；再轮换，p 在右边。<bookmark mark='c'/>真正的答案是右边，每次都是。<bookmark mark='d'/>这不是罕见的意外：在这条直线附近，成千上万个最近的浮点数点得到互相矛盾的答案，而建立在矛盾答案上的算法会崩溃、陷入死循环，或者返回一个不凸的凸包。

ad01e80af44f.en: Kettner and his colleagues drew the picture in 2008. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take every float within two hundred and fifty-six steps of one half, one half, a grid of sixty-five thousand points, and colour each by what floating point says: blue for left, green for right, grey for on the line. The true line runs exactly along the diagonal. <bookmark mark='b'/> Instead of a clean split, a speckled band. <bookmark mark='c'/> Mark the wrong answers in red: nearly twelve thousand. This part starts by fixing that test, and then builds on it the beautiful structures of the plane.
ad01e80af44f.zh: Kettner 和他的同事们在2008年画出了这幅图。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一半、一半周围二百五十六个步长之内的所有浮点数，一个六万五千点的网格，按浮点运算的回答给每个点上色：左边蓝色，右边绿色，线上灰色。真正的直线恰好沿着对角线。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们看到的不是干净的分界，而是一条斑驳的带子。<bookmark mark='c'/>把错误的答案标成红色：将近一万二千个。这一部分先修好这个测试，再在它之上构造平面上那些美丽的结构。

e8e537342f98.en: Part 22 of Computer Science, Built: Geometry. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the orientation test, made exact at almost no cost; convex hulls, the sweep line, and guards for an art gallery; Voronoi diagrams grown by a sweep of parabolas, and Delaunay triangulations, which turn out to be the shadow of a three-dimensional hull; randomized algorithms and the backwards analysis that prices them; linear programming, range search, point location and the curse of high dimensions; and motion planning for a robot.
e8e537342f98.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第22部分：几何。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：几乎不花代价就变得精确的方向测试；凸包、扫描线，以及美术馆的守卫；由抛物线扫描生长出的 Voronoi 图，和原来是三维凸包之投影的 Delaunay 三角剖分；随机化算法和为它们定价的反向分析；线性规划、范围查询、点定位和高维的诅咒；以及为机器人规划运动。

638f90c3602b.en: Almost every algorithm in this part asks one question, over and over. <bookmark mark='a'/> Walk from p to q; is r on your left? The answer is the sign of a two by two determinant built from the differences of the coordinates. <bookmark mark='b'/> The determinant is twice the signed area of the triangle p q r: <bookmark mark='c'/> positive when the three points turn counter-clockwise, <bookmark mark='d'/> negative when they turn clockwise, and zero when they lie on one line. <bookmark mark='e'/> Convex hulls, sweeps, triangulations and point-in-polygon tests are all built from this sign. <bookmark mark='f'/> Its cousin, the in-circle test, asks whether a point lies inside the circle through three others; it is a three by three determinant, and we will meet it with Delaunay.
638f90c3602b.zh: 这一部分几乎每个算法都在一遍又一遍地问同一个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>从 p 走向 q，r 在你的左边吗？答案是一个由坐标之差构成的二乘二行列式的符号。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个行列式是三角形 p q r 有向面积的两倍：<bookmark mark='c'/>三点逆时针转时为正，<bookmark mark='d'/>顺时针转时为负，共线时为零。<bookmark mark='e'/>凸包、扫描、三角剖分和点在多边形内的测试，都由这个符号构成。<bookmark mark='f'/>它的近亲内圆测试问的是一个点是否在过另外三点的圆内；它是一个三乘三行列式，我们会在 Delaunay 那里遇到它。

4f6225f8a50b.en: Why does it fail? <bookmark mark='a'/> The determinant is a difference of two products, a minus b. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each subtraction and each product is rounded to the nearest double, with a relative error of about one part in nine million billion. <bookmark mark='c'/> Near a line, a and b are almost equal, and their difference is tiny: smaller than the rounding errors made computing them. The sign of the result is then noise. <bookmark mark='d'/> But the error can be bounded. Jonathan Shewchuk proved that it is at most about three epsilon times the sizes of a and b. <bookmark mark='e'/> So when the computed answer is bigger than that bound, its sign is certainly right. <bookmark mark='f'/> When it isn't, ignoring the problem is dangerous: Kettner's paper shows the textbook incremental hull losing points, looping, and returning a polygon that is not convex.
4f6225f8a50b.zh: 它为什么会出错？<bookmark mark='a'/>行列式是两个乘积之差，a 减 b。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次减法和乘法都被舍入到最近的双精度数，相对误差约为九百万亿分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>在直线附近，a 和 b 几乎相等，它们的差极小：比计算它们时产生的舍入误差还小。这时结果的符号就是噪声。<bookmark mark='d'/>但误差可以被界住。Jonathan Shewchuk 证明，误差至多约为三个 epsilon 乘以 a 和 b 的大小。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以当算出的答案大于这个界时，它的符号一定是对的。<bookmark mark='f'/>否则，忽视这个问题是危险的：Kettner 的论文展示了教科书上的增量凸包丢失点、陷入循环，以及返回不凸的多边形。

fb55c08f9cf0.en: That gives Shewchuk's adaptive predicates. <bookmark mark='a'/> Compute the determinant in floating point. <bookmark mark='b'/> If it is bigger than the error bound, stop: the sign is certain. <bookmark mark='c'/> Otherwise compute it again exactly. Shewchuk does this with expansions, sums of doubles that carry every lost bit; we use rational numbers, which are slower but simple. <bookmark mark='d'/> We measured twenty thousand tests of each kind. On random points, plain floating point is never wrong, and the adaptive test never needs its exact stage, so it costs about twice a bare multiplication. On nearly collinear points, floating point is wrong almost one time in five, and the adaptive test falls back to exact arithmetic seven times in ten. <bookmark mark='e'/> The point is that you pay for exactness only where the answer is in doubt. <bookmark mark='f'/> Another route is to keep coordinates as small integers, for which the computation is exact; the algorithms in this part do that, with Python's unbounded integers.
fb55c08f9cf0.zh: 这就得到了 Shewchuk 的自适应谓词。<bookmark mark='a'/>先用浮点数计算行列式。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果它大于误差界，就停下：符号是确定的。<bookmark mark='c'/>否则就精确地再算一遍。Shewchuk 用扩展表示，即保存每一个丢失比特的双精度数之和；我们用有理数，慢一些但简单。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们对每种输入各测了两万次。在随机点上，普通浮点数从不出错，自适应测试也从不需要精确阶段，所以代价大约是一次裸乘法的两倍。在几乎共线的点上，浮点数差不多五次错一次，而自适应测试十次中有七次退回到精确运算。<bookmark mark='e'/>关键在于，只在答案可疑的地方才为精确性付费。<bookmark mark='f'/>另一条路是让坐标保持为小整数，这时计算本身就是精确的；这一部分的算法就是这样做的，用 Python 的无界整数。

81c82f0a5c04.en: The convex hull of a set of points is the smallest convex polygon that contains them all: stretch a rubber band around nails and let go. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ronald Graham's scan, from 1972, starts at the lowest point, <bookmark mark='b'/> sorts the others by the angle they make with it, <bookmark mark='c'/> and walks through them in that order, keeping the hull so far on a stack. Each new point is pushed; but first, while the last two points on the stack and the new one turn clockwise, the last point cannot be on the hull, and is popped. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every point is pushed once and popped at most once, so after sorting the walk is linear. <bookmark mark='e'/> Graham needed it at Bell Labs, for a plotter drawing ten thousand points.
81c82f0a5c04.zh: 一组点的凸包是包含它们全部的最小凸多边形：在钉子周围套上橡皮筋，然后松手。<bookmark mark='a'/>Ronald Graham 1972年的扫描从最低点出发，<bookmark mark='b'/>按其他点与它所成的角度排序，<bookmark mark='c'/>再按这个顺序走过它们，把目前的凸包保存在栈上。每个新点都要压入；但在此之前，只要栈顶两点与新点构成顺时针转向，栈顶那个点就不可能在凸包上，于是弹出。<bookmark mark='d'/>每个点压入一次、至多弹出一次，所以排序之后这一遍是线性的。<bookmark mark='e'/>Graham 在贝尔实验室需要它，为一台要画一万个点的绘图仪。

315879e8941d.en: We implemented five hull algorithms with counters, and ran each on ten thousand points drawn from a square, from a disk, and from a circle. <bookmark mark='a'/> The hull of random points in a square has only about twenty vertices; in a disk, about seventy-five; on a circle, every point is on the hull. <bookmark mark='b'/> Jarvis's gift wrapping, from 1973, finds one hull vertex per round by checking every point, n times h tests: cheap on the square, hopeless on the circle. <bookmark mark='c'/> Graham's scan and Andrew's monotone chain, which sorts by x and builds the lower and upper hulls separately, cost about n log n whatever the shape, almost all of it sorting. <bookmark mark='d'/> Quickhull splits the points like quicksort, and like quicksort it is fast on random input and quadratic on bad input. <bookmark mark='e'/> Timothy Chan's algorithm, from 1996, needs only n log h, which is optimal, but its constant factor is large. At these sizes the monotone chain wins, and it is what most libraries use.
315879e8941d.zh: 我们实现了五个带计数器的凸包算法，在一万个分别取自正方形、圆盘和圆周的点上运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>正方形中随机点的凸包只有大约二十个顶点；圆盘中约七十五个；在圆周上，每个点都在凸包上。<bookmark mark='b'/>Jarvis 1973年的礼品包装法每一轮检查所有点找到一个凸包顶点，共 n 乘 h 次测试：在正方形上很便宜，在圆周上毫无希望。<bookmark mark='c'/>Graham 扫描和 Andrew 的单调链（按 x 排序，分别构造下凸包和上凸包），无论形状如何都大约花 n log n，几乎全花在排序上。<bookmark mark='d'/>快速凸包像快速排序那样划分点集，也像快速排序一样：随机输入上快，坏输入上是平方级。<bookmark mark='e'/>Timothy Chan 1996年的算法只需要 n log h，这是最优的，但它的常数因子很大。在这些规模下单调链胜出，大多数程序库用的也是它。

a23e679aaae4.en: Could a cleverer algorithm avoid the n log n? No, and the proof is a reduction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose you want to sort some numbers. Lift each number x to the point x, x squared. <bookmark mark='b'/> All the lifted points lie on a parabola, which is convex, so every one of them is a vertex of the hull. <bookmark mark='c'/> Walk around the hull from the leftmost point and you meet them in sorted order. <bookmark mark='d'/> So any hull algorithm is also a sorting algorithm, with linear extra work. Part 16 proved that sorting by comparisons needs n log n; Michael Ben-Or extended the bound in 1983 to algorithms that compute with arithmetic and test signs, which is what hull algorithms do.
a23e679aaae4.zh: 更聪明的算法能避开 n log n 吗？不能，证明是一个归约。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设你想给一些数排序。把每个数 x 提升为点 x、x 的平方。<bookmark mark='b'/>所有提升后的点都在一条抛物线上，而抛物线是凸的，所以它们每一个都是凸包的顶点。<bookmark mark='c'/>从最左点出发绕凸包走一圈，你就按排好的顺序遇到它们。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以任何凸包算法也是一个排序算法，只多线性的额外工作。第16部分证明了基于比较的排序需要 n log n；Michael Ben-Or 在1983年把这个界推广到用算术计算并检验符号的算法，而凸包算法正是这样做的。

e58351fb6844.en: There is a loophole. <bookmark mark='a'/> The lower bound needs every point on the hull. When the hull has only h vertices, can we pay n log h? <bookmark mark='b'/> Timothy Chan's algorithm splits the points into groups of m and finds each group's hull with Graham's scan. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then it wraps the whole set like Jarvis: to find the next vertex, it asks each small hull for its tangent from the current point, which a binary search answers in log m steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> If m equals h, that is h rounds of n over m times log m, and n log h in all. <bookmark mark='e'/> We don't know h, so Chan guesses: m equal to four, then sixteen, then two hundred and fifty-six, squaring each time, and abandons a guess after m rounds. The failed guesses form a geometric series and cost nothing extra in order. <bookmark mark='f'/> Kirkpatrick and Seidel reached n log h first, in 1986, under the title The ultimate planar convex hull algorithm. In three dimensions the hull still costs n log n, with the randomized method of chapter eight.
e58351fb6844.zh: 这里有一个漏洞。<bookmark mark='a'/>下界要求每个点都在凸包上。当凸包只有 h 个顶点时，能只付 n log h 吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>Chan 的算法把点分成每组 m 个，用 Graham 扫描求出每组的凸包。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后像 Jarvis 那样包裹整个点集：为了找下一个顶点，它向每个小凸包询问从当前点出发的切线，二分查找用 log m 步就能回答。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果 m 等于 h，就是 h 轮、每轮 n 除以 m 乘 log m，总共 n log h。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们不知道 h，所以Chan 去猜：m 取四，然后十六，然后二百五十六，每次平方，在 m 轮之后放弃这个猜测。失败的猜测构成一个几何级数，在阶上不增加任何代价。<bookmark mark='f'/>Kirkpatrick 与 Seidel 在1986年最先达到 n log h，论文题为《终极平面凸包算法》。在三维中凸包仍需 n log n，用的是第八章的随机化方法。

f4e1fdec6e55.en: Given n line segments, which pairs cross? Testing every pair takes n squared tests, even when almost nothing crosses. <bookmark mark='a'/> Jon Bentley and Thomas Ottmann, in 1979, swept a vertical line across the plane from left to right. It stops only at events: the endpoints of segments, and crossings, once they have been predicted. <bookmark mark='b'/> Along the way it keeps the status: the segments the line currently meets, ordered from top to bottom. <bookmark mark='c'/> The key observation is that two segments can only cross after they become neighbours in that order, so we only ever test neighbours: when a segment arrives, against the two beside it; when one leaves, the two it separated; and at a crossing, the two that swap places meet new neighbours. <bookmark mark='d'/> Watch the line move. Each crossing is found by a test made when its two segments first became adjacent, and at the crossing they trade places in the status. <bookmark mark='e'/> With a balanced tree for the status and a heap for the events, the cost is n plus k, times log n, for k crossings.
f4e1fdec6e55.zh: 给定 n 条线段，哪些对相交？检查每一对要 n 平方次测试，即使几乎没有相交。<bookmark mark='a'/>1979年，Jon Bentley 与 Thomas Ottmann 让一条竖直线从左到右扫过平面。它只在事件处停下：线段的端点，以及已被预测出的交点。<bookmark mark='b'/>一路上它维护状态：扫描线当前碰到的线段，从上到下排好序。<bookmark mark='c'/>关键的观察是，两条线段只有在状态中成为邻居之后才可能相交，所以我们只测试邻居：一条线段到来时，测它和两旁的；离开时，测被它隔开的两条；在交点处，交换位置的两条遇到新邻居。<bookmark mark='d'/>看扫描线移动。每个交点都是在它的两条线段刚成为邻居时做的一次测试中被发现的，到了交点它们在状态中交换位置。<bookmark mark='e'/>用平衡树存状态、用堆存事件，代价是 n 加 k 再乘 log n，k 为交点数。

42f87c87c912.en: We ran our sweep on short random segments in the unit square, from a hundred to three thousand, and checked it against testing every pair. <bookmark mark='a'/> The number of events is always exactly two per segment plus one per crossing, and the pair tests are about twice the events: for three thousand segments, twenty thousand tests instead of four and a half million. <bookmark mark='b'/> Bernard Chazelle and Herbert Edelsbrunner later shaved the bound to n log n plus k, which is optimal. <bookmark mark='c'/> The idea outlives the problem. A sweep turns a two-dimensional question into a sequence of one-dimensional ones, and chapter five sweeps a line over a set of points to build a Voronoi diagram. <bookmark mark='d'/> Sweeps compute the overlay of map layers in geographic systems, check the design rules of chips, and take unions and intersections of polygons in CAD.
42f87c87c912.zh: 我们在单位正方形中的随机短线段上运行我们的扫描，从一百条到三千条，并与检查每一对的结果核对。<bookmark mark='a'/>事件数总是恰好每条线段两个、每个交点一个，而成对测试大约是事件数的两倍：三千条线段只要两万次测试，而不是四百五十万次。<bookmark mark='b'/>Bernard Chazelle 与 Herbert Edelsbrunner 后来把界削减到 n log n 加 k，这是最优的。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个想法比这个问题活得更久。扫描把一个二维问题变成一串一维问题，第五章将用一条扫过点集的线来构造 Voronoi 图。<bookmark mark='d'/>扫描用来计算地理信息系统中地图图层的叠加、检查芯片的设计规则，以及在 CAD 中求多边形的并与交。

2ab4f3d105dd.en: Chapter four. Guarding an art gallery.

2f6aa12f3e9c.en: In 1973 Victor Klee asked a question about museums. A gallery is a polygon with n walls; a guard stands at one point and sees in every direction. How many guards are enough for any gallery with n walls? <bookmark mark='a'/> Václav Chvátal proved in 1975 that n over three always suffice, rounded down, and that sometimes that many are needed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is why some galleries need them: a comb. Each tooth's tip can be seen only from inside that tooth, so every tooth needs its own guard, and a comb with k teeth has three k plus two walls.
2f6aa12f3e9c.zh: 1973年，Victor Klee 提出了一个关于博物馆的问题。美术馆是一个有 n 面墙的多边形；守卫站在一点，向各个方向看。对任意有 n 面墙的美术馆，多少名守卫就够了？<bookmark mark='a'/>Václav Chvátal 在1975年证明，n 除以三（向下取整）名总是足够，而且有时恰好需要这么多。<bookmark mark='b'/>这里说明为什么有些美术馆需要这么多：一把梳子。每个齿的尖端只能从那个齿内部看到，所以每个齿都需要自己的守卫，而有 k 个齿的梳子有三 k 加二面墙。

0884f7a11dd9.en: Steve Fisk found a proof in 1978 that fits on a postcard. <bookmark mark='a'/> First triangulate the gallery with diagonals. That is always possible: Gary Meisters showed every polygon has an ear, three consecutive corners whose triangle lies inside, and cutting ears one by one triangulates it. <bookmark mark='b'/> The triangles, joined across diagonals, form a tree. Colour the corners of one triangle blue, green and yellow; each neighbouring triangle shares two coloured corners, so its third has only one colour left. Walking the tree colours every corner, and every triangle gets all three colours. <bookmark mark='c'/> Some colour is used at most n over three times. <bookmark mark='d'/> Put a guard on every corner of that colour. Each triangle has one, and a triangle is seen entirely from any of its corners, so the whole gallery is watched.
0884f7a11dd9.zh: Steve Fisk 在1978年找到一个写得进明信片的证明。<bookmark mark='a'/>先用对角线把美术馆三角剖分。这总是可行的：Gary Meisters 证明了每个多边形都有一只耳朵，即三个相邻顶点所成的三角形位于多边形内部，一只一只地切下耳朵就完成三角剖分。<bookmark mark='b'/>沿对角线相连的三角形构成一棵树。把一个三角形的三个顶点涂成蓝、绿、黄；每个相邻三角形共享两个已着色的顶点，所以它的第三个顶点只剩一种颜色。走遍这棵树就给每个顶点着了色，而每个三角形都得到全部三种颜色。<bookmark mark='c'/>某种颜色至多用了 n 除以三次。<bookmark mark='d'/>在这种颜色的每个顶点上放一名守卫。每个三角形都有一名，而一个三角形从它的任何顶点都能被完全看到，所以整个美术馆都被看守住了。

75c6b6624595.en: How fast can we triangulate? <bookmark mark='a'/> Ear clipping is quadratic. <bookmark mark='b'/> Splitting the polygon into monotone pieces, which a stack triangulates in linear time, gives n log n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bernard Chazelle found a linear-time algorithm in 1991, a landmark so intricate that nobody implements it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Fisk's argument gives a guard set, not the smallest one: on two hundred random polygons with sixty corners, the smallest colour class averaged seventeen guards. <bookmark mark='e'/> Finding the true minimum is NP-hard, and in 2018 it was shown to be as hard as deciding statements about real numbers, a class just above NP. <bookmark mark='f'/> Behind the puzzle are camera placement, sensor coverage, and the triangulation of every polygon a graphics card draws.
75c6b6624595.zh: 三角剖分能有多快？<bookmark mark='a'/>切耳朵是平方级的。<bookmark mark='b'/>把多边形分成单调的块，每块用一个栈在线性时间内三角剖分，得到 n log n。<bookmark mark='c'/>Bernard Chazelle 在1991年找到线性时间算法，这个里程碑复杂到没有人去实现它。<bookmark mark='d'/>Fisk 的论证给出一组守卫，而不是最少的一组：在两百个有六十个顶点的随机多边形上，最小的颜色类平均有十七名守卫。<bookmark mark='e'/>求真正的最小值是 NP 难的，2018年还证明了它和判定实数命题一样难，那是一个比 NP 略高的类。<bookmark mark='f'/>这个谜题背后是摄像头的布置、传感器的覆盖，以及显卡绘制的每个多边形的三角剖分。

1acae9d5d63e.en: Scatter n post offices over a city. For every address, which one is nearest? <bookmark mark='a'/> The answer divides the plane into regions, one per site: the Voronoi diagram. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its edges are the points equally far from two sites, pieces of their perpendicular bisectors. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its vertices are equally far from three, the centres of circles through three sites with no site inside. <bookmark mark='d'/> Euler's formula keeps it small: at most two n minus five vertices and three n minus six edges. <bookmark mark='e'/> Dirichlet used it in 1850 and Georgy Voronoi in 1908; John Snow's map of the 1854 cholera outbreak in London is a Voronoi diagram of water pumps.
1acae9d5d63e.zh: 在一座城市里散布 n 个邮局。对每个地址，哪一个最近？<bookmark mark='a'/>答案把平面分成区域，每个站点一个：Voronoi 图。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的边是到两个站点等距的点，即它们垂直平分线的一段。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的顶点到三个站点等距，是过三个站点且内部没有站点的圆的圆心。<bookmark mark='d'/>欧拉公式让它保持很小：至多二 n 减五个顶点和三 n 减六条边。<bookmark mark='e'/>Dirichlet 在1850年用过它，Georgy Voronoi 在1908年；John Snow 的1854年伦敦霍乱地图就是一张水泵的 Voronoi 图。

084655fb1194.en: Steven Fortune found, in 1986, a way to build the diagram with a sweep. The difficulty is that a line sweeping down meets a Voronoi region before it meets the region's site, so it cannot know yet what lies below. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fortune's answer: consider the points that are as close to a site above the line as to the line itself. For each site, they form a parabola. <bookmark mark='b'/> The lowest of these parabolas form the beach line. Any point above it is closer to some site than to the sweep line, so no site still below the line can claim it: above the beach line, the diagram is final. <bookmark mark='c'/> As the line moves, the breakpoints where arcs meet slide along Voronoi edges and draw them. <bookmark mark='d'/> When the line reaches a site, a new arc is born, a thin spike that widens. <bookmark mark='e'/> When an arc shrinks to nothing between its neighbours, three sites are equally far from one point and from the line: that point is a Voronoi vertex, and the line touches the bottom of the empty circle through the three sites. <bookmark mark='f'/> Those are the only two events, so with a balanced tree for the beach line the sweep takes n log n.
084655fb1194.zh: 1986年，Steven Fortune 找到了用扫描构造这个图的方法。难点在于，向下扫的直线在遇到一个区域的站点之前就先遇到了这个区域，所以它还无法知道下面有什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>Fortune 的回答是：考虑那些到扫描线上方某个站点与到扫描线本身一样近的点。对每个站点，它们构成一条抛物线。<bookmark mark='b'/>这些抛物线中最低的部分构成海滩线。海滩线上方的任何点都比扫描线更靠近某个站点，所以仍在扫描线下方的站点都不可能占有它：在海滩线上方，图已经是最终的了。<bookmark mark='c'/>随着扫描线移动，弧与弧相接的断点沿 Voronoi 边滑动，把边画出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>扫描线到达一个站点时，诞生一条新弧，一根逐渐变宽的细刺。<bookmark mark='e'/>当一条弧在两个邻居之间缩成零，三个站点到某一点的距离与到扫描线的距离都相等：那一点就是 Voronoi 顶点，扫描线恰好碰到过这三个站点的空圆的底部。<bookmark mark='f'/>只有这两种事件，所以用平衡树存海滩线，扫描只需 n log n。

1463139bd8e9.en: We implemented the sweep, with the beach line kept as a simple list, and ran it on up to two thousand random sites. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every Voronoi vertex is exactly one circle event, and there are always two n minus two minus h of them, where h is the number of sites on the convex hull. <bookmark mark='b'/> Many more circle events are scheduled than happen: when a new arc arrives under a shrinking one, the predicted vertex is a false alarm and is cancelled. <bookmark mark='c'/> The three sites of each vertex form a triangle of the Delaunay triangulation, the subject of the next chapter, and our triangles agree exactly with a completely different method, the lifting map of chapter seven. <bookmark mark='d'/> A plain list makes our sweep quadratic; a balanced tree makes it n log n.
1463139bd8e9.zh: 我们实现了这个扫描，海滩线存为一个简单的列表，并在多达两千个随机站点上运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个 Voronoi 顶点恰好是一个圆事件，而它们总是有二 n 减二减 h 个，h 为凸包上的站点数。<bookmark mark='b'/>安排的圆事件远多于真正发生的：当一条新弧来到一条正在缩小的弧之下，预测的顶点就成了误报，被取消。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个顶点的三个站点构成 Delaunay 三角剖分的一个三角形，即下一章的主题；我们的三角形与一种完全不同的方法，第七章的提升映射，结果完全一致。<bookmark mark='d'/>普通列表使我们的扫描成为平方级；平衡树使它成为 n log n。

3f38e5421dc8.en: Connect the sites with triangles. There are many ways; which is best? <bookmark mark='a'/> Boris Delaunay's answer, from 1934: join three sites whenever the circle through them has no other site inside. <bookmark mark='b'/> Those circles are exactly the empty circles of the Voronoi vertices, so the Delaunay triangulation is the Voronoi diagram's dual: an edge for every pair of neighbouring regions. <bookmark mark='c'/> Whether a point lies inside a circle through three others is decided by a sign, the in-circle test, a three by three determinant with squared distances in its last column. Like the orientation test, it can be made exact.
3f38e5421dc8.zh: 用三角形把站点连起来。方法有很多；哪一种最好？<bookmark mark='a'/>Boris Delaunay 1934年的回答：只要过三个站点的圆内没有其他站点，就把它们连起来。<bookmark mark='b'/>这些圆恰好就是 Voronoi 顶点的空圆，所以 Delaunay 三角剖分是 Voronoi 图的对偶：每对相邻区域对应一条边。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个点是否在过另外三点的圆内，由一个符号决定，即内圆测试，一个最后一列为距离平方的三乘三行列式。和方向测试一样，它也可以做到精确。

7bd405f6e630.en: How do we find it? Charles Lawson's method, from 1977, starts from any triangulation at all. <bookmark mark='a'/> This one connects the points as a sweep from left to right meets them, and it is full of slivers: <bookmark mark='b'/> its thinnest angle is under half a degree. <bookmark mark='c'/> Look at two triangles sharing an edge. If the far corner of one lies inside the circle of the other, the edge is illegal; flip it, replacing it with the other diagonal of the quadrilateral. Repeat. <bookmark mark='d'/> Seventeen flips later no edge is illegal, and what is left is the Delaunay triangulation. <bookmark mark='e'/> Its smallest angle has grown tenfold, and Robin Sibson proved that among all triangulations of the points, Delaunay's maximizes the smallest angle. <bookmark mark='f'/> Why does flipping ever stop? The next chapter will show that each flip pushes down a surface in three dimensions, which cannot go down forever.
7bd405f6e630.zh: 怎样找到它？Charles Lawson 1977年的方法可以从任意三角剖分出发。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一个按从左到右的扫描遇到点的顺序把它们连起来，满是细长的三角形：<bookmark mark='b'/>它最小的角不到半度。<bookmark mark='c'/>看两个共享一条边的三角形。如果一个三角形的远端顶点落在另一个三角形的外接圆内，这条边就是不合法的；翻转它，换成四边形的另一条对角线。重复。<bookmark mark='d'/>十七次翻转之后，没有不合法的边了，剩下的就是 Delaunay 三角剖分。<bookmark mark='e'/>它的最小角增大了十倍，而 Robin Sibson 证明，在这些点的所有三角剖分中，Delaunay 的使最小角最大。<bookmark mark='f'/>翻转为什么总会停止？下一章会说明，每次翻转都把三维中的一个曲面往下压，而它不可能无限地降下去。

fbea552544d3.en: The empty circles are worth having. <bookmark mark='a'/> A triangulation without needless slivers is what simulations need: finite-element meshes are Delaunay, refined by adding points, as in Jim Ruppert's algorithm. <bookmark mark='b'/> Terrain models join scattered height measurements this way, and the triangulation gives natural interpolation between them. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it holds the answers to other questions: each point's nearest neighbour is joined to it by a Delaunay edge, and so is every edge of the minimum spanning tree, as we are about to check. <bookmark mark='e'/> It can be built in n log n three ways: by Fortune's sweep, by divide and conquer, or, most simply, by inserting the points in random order, which is the next chapter but one.
fbea552544d3.zh: 空圆是值得拥有的。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有多余细长三角形的剖分正是模拟所需要的：有限元网格就是 Delaunay 网格，再通过加点来加密，如 Jim Ruppert 的算法。<bookmark mark='b'/>地形模型用这种方式连接散布的高程测量，而三角剖分给出了它们之间自然的插值。<bookmark mark='c'/>它还藏着其他问题的答案：每个点与它的最近邻之间有一条 Delaunay 边，最小生成树的每条边也是如此，我们马上就来核对。<bookmark mark='e'/>它可以用三种方法在 n log n 内构造：Fortune 的扫描、分治，或者最简单的，按随机顺序插入点，这是下下章的内容。

319d25f8578d.en: Here is the claim tested. <bookmark mark='a'/> Seventy points, their Delaunay triangulation in grey, and in green their minimum spanning tree, the shortest network that connects them all. Every green edge lies on a grey one. <bookmark mark='b'/> The reason is an exchange argument: if a tree edge a b were not a Delaunay edge, some point would sit inside the circle with a b as diameter, closer to both ends, and swapping it in would make the tree shorter. <bookmark mark='c'/> So Kruskal's algorithm from Part 18 need only look at the Delaunay edges, about three per point. For eight thousand points that is twenty-four thousand edges instead of thirty-two million pairs, and the tree comes out identical to Prim's algorithm run on every pair. Michael Shamos and Dan Hoey made this the first n log n algorithm for the problem in 1975.
319d25f8578d.zh: 来检验这个说法。<bookmark mark='a'/>七十个点，灰色是它们的 Delaunay 三角剖分，绿色是它们的最小生成树，即连接所有点的最短网络。每条绿边都落在一条灰边上。<bookmark mark='b'/>原因是一个交换论证：如果树边 a b 不是 Delaunay 边，就会有某个点落在以 a b 为直径的圆内，离两端都更近，把它换进来会让树更短。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以第18部分的 Kruskal 算法只需看 Delaunay 边，大约每点三条。对八千个点，这是两万四千条边而不是三千二百万对，而得到的树与在所有点对上运行 Prim 算法的结果完全相同。Michael Shamos 与 Dan Hoey 在1975年由此给出了这个问题的第一个 n log n 算法。

2952b0807eb4.en: Here is the most beautiful fact in this part. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the Delaunay triangulation of some points, seen from above. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now lift every point straight up, onto the paraboloid z equals x squared plus y squared. <bookmark mark='c'/> The lifted points sit on a convex bowl, so all of them are on the three-dimensional convex hull. Look at the hull from below: its faces are triangles. <bookmark mark='d'/> Why those triangles? Take a circle in the plane. Its points, lifted, all lie on one plane, because on the circle x squared plus y squared is a linear function of x and y. <bookmark mark='e'/> A point inside the circle lifts to below that plane, and a point outside lifts to above it. <bookmark mark='f'/> So a circle through three sites is empty exactly when every other lifted point is above the plane through those three: exactly when the three lifted points form a face of the lower hull. <bookmark mark='g'/> The Delaunay triangulation is the shadow of the lower convex hull of the lifted points. Kevin Brown saw it in 1979, and it holds in every dimension: Delaunay in d dimensions is a hull in d plus one.
2952b0807eb4.zh: 这是这一部分最美的事实。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一些点的 Delaunay 三角剖分，从上方看。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在把每个点竖直向上提升到抛物面 z 等于 x 平方加 y 平方上。<bookmark mark='c'/>提升后的点位于一只凸碗上，所以它们全都在三维凸包上。从下方看这个凸包：它的面都是三角形。<bookmark mark='d'/>为什么是这些三角形？取平面上的一个圆。它的点提升之后全都落在同一个平面上，因为在圆上 x 平方加 y 平方是 x 和 y 的线性函数。<bookmark mark='e'/>圆内的点提升后在那个平面之下，圆外的点提升后在它之上。<bookmark mark='f'/>所以过三个站点的圆是空的，恰好当其余所有提升点都在过这三点的平面之上：恰好当这三个提升点构成下凸包的一个面。<bookmark mark='g'/>Delaunay 三角剖分是提升点下凸包的投影。Kevin Brown 在1979年看出了这一点，而且它在每个维度都成立：d 维的 Delaunay 就是 d 加一维中的凸包。

cd7623cfc93f.en: The lifting map also explains the in-circle test. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the coordinates of four points with their lifted heights in a four by four determinant. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is the orientation test in three dimensions, the sign of a volume, asking whether d's lifted point lies below the plane through the other three. <bookmark mark='c'/> For one example the four by four determinant and chapter six's three by three both come out at ninety-six, because subtracting the last row reduces one to the other. <bookmark mark='d'/> It also finishes chapter six: a Lawson flip replaces an edge where the lifted surface bends up with one where it bends down, so the surface drops with every flip, and since there are only finitely many triangulations, flipping stops. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the Voronoi diagram is the same picture turned over: lift each site to a plane tangent to the paraboloid, and the Voronoi regions are the shadows of the faces of their upper envelope. <bookmark mark='f'/> We checked the theorem: the lower faces of scipy's hull of our lifted points are exactly scipy's Delaunay triangulation.
cd7623cfc93f.zh: 提升映射也解释了内圆测试。<bookmark mark='a'/>把四个点的坐标连同提升后的高度写成一个四乘四行列式。<bookmark mark='b'/>它就是三维中的方向测试，一个体积的符号，问 d 的提升点是否在过其余三点的平面之下。<bookmark mark='c'/>在一个例子中，四乘四行列式和第六章的三乘三行列式都等于九十六，因为减去最后一行就把一个化成另一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>它也补完了第六章：一次 Lawson 翻转把提升曲面向上弯的一条边换成向下弯的一条，所以每次翻转曲面都下降；而三角剖分只有有限多个，所以翻转一定会停止。<bookmark mark='e'/>Voronoi 图则是把同一幅图翻过来：把每个站点提升为与抛物面相切的平面，Voronoi 区域就是它们上包络各个面的投影。<bookmark mark='f'/>我们核对了这个定理：scipy 对我们的提升点所求凸包的下表面，恰好就是 scipy 的 Delaunay 三角剖分。

5b3b91feb58f.en: Chapter eight. Random order and backwards analysis.
5b3b91feb58f.zh: 第8章。随机顺序与反向分析。

08c19eb190a3.en: The simplest way to build a Delaunay triangulation is to add the points one at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a triangulation, and a new point to insert. First find the triangle that contains it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then find every triangle whose empty circle the new point spoils, the triangles in conflict with it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Remove them all, leaving a hole shaped like a star around the new point, and join the new point to every corner of the hole. <bookmark mark='d'/> The number of new triangles is the new point's degree. <bookmark mark='e'/> Lawson's flips, starting from the triangle that contains the point, carry out exactly this change one edge at a time. The question is what the whole sequence of insertions costs.
08c19eb190a3.zh: 构造 Delaunay 三角剖分最简单的方法是一次加一个点。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里是一个三角剖分，以及一个要插入的新点。先找到包含它的三角形。<bookmark mark='b'/>再找出所有空圆被新点破坏的三角形，即与它冲突的三角形。<bookmark mark='c'/>把它们全部移除，留下一个围绕新点的星形空洞，再把新点连到空洞的每个顶点。<bookmark mark='d'/>新三角形的个数就是新点的度。<bookmark mark='e'/>从包含该点的三角形出发做 Lawson 翻转，一次一条边地完成的正是这个变化。问题是整个插入序列的代价是多少。

5671e15953e4.en: In a bad order, a single insertion can change almost everything: a point can arrive connected to all i points before it, and the total becomes quadratic. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a random order, a beautiful argument shows it cannot. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run the algorithm backwards. Look at the triangulation after i insertions. Because the order is random, the point inserted last is equally likely to be any of the i points present. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its expected degree is the average degree of the triangulation, twice the number of edges over i, <bookmark mark='d'/> and Euler's formula says a planar triangulation has fewer than three i edges. <bookmark mark='e'/> So the average degree is below six, and each insertion creates fewer than six new triangles on average, whatever the points. <bookmark mark='f'/> Finding where each point goes costs n log n in expectation, by the same argument applied to lists of conflicts, which Kenneth Clarkson and Peter Shor introduced in 1989. <bookmark mark='g'/> Raimund Seidel named the trick backwards analysis. It prices randomized quicksort, treaps and the linear programming of the next chapter in exactly the same way.
5671e15953e4.zh: 在坏的顺序下，一次插入可能改变几乎一切：一个点到来时可能与之前的全部 i 个点相连，总代价就成了平方级。<bookmark mark='a'/>在随机顺序下，一个漂亮的论证表明不会如此。<bookmark mark='b'/>把算法倒过来运行。看插入 i 个点之后的三角剖分。因为顺序是随机的，最后插入的点等可能是现有 i 个点中的任何一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的期望度就是三角剖分的平均度，即边数的两倍除以 i，<bookmark mark='d'/>而欧拉公式说平面三角剖分的边数少于三 i。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以平均度小于六，每次插入平均新建不到六个三角形，无论点是什么。<bookmark mark='f'/>找到每个点的位置期望花费 n log n，用同样的论证作用于冲突列表，这是 Kenneth Clarkson 与 Peter Shor 在1989年引入的。<bookmark mark='g'/>Raimund Seidel 给这个技巧取名为反向分析。它以完全相同的方式为随机化快速排序、树堆以及下一章的线性规划定价。

ef73b5ab62eb.en: We counted the triangles our incremental algorithm creates. <bookmark mark='a'/> On random points, inserted in random order, it is about nine per point at every size, just under the bound of nine n plus one, with about three flips per point. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then a set built to be bad: a long, nearly flat convex chain, followed by points above its middle, inserted from the top down, so that each new point is joined to the whole chain. In that order the work grows quadratically: for sixteen hundred points, eight hundred and seventy thousand triangles. <bookmark mark='c'/> Shuffle the same points, and it is thirteen thousand again, eight per point. The shuffle costs one line of code, and the guarantee holds for every input.
ef73b5ab62eb.zh: 我们统计了增量算法创建的三角形。<bookmark mark='a'/>在随机点、随机顺序下，每种规模都是大约每点九个，略低于九 n 加一的界，每点大约三次翻转。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是一个特意构造的坏集合：一条又长又几乎平直的凸链，再加上它中间上方的点，自上而下插入，使每个新点都与整条链相连。按那个顺序，工作量呈平方增长：一千六百个点要创建八十七万个三角形。<bookmark mark='c'/>把同样的点打乱，又回到一万三千个，每点八个。打乱只需一行代码，而保证对每个输入都成立。

232dd9f07c6f.en: Chapter nine. Linear programming in the plane.
232dd9f07c6f.zh: 第9章。平面上的线性规划。

f4a69ad1e9cf.en: A linear program asks for the point of a convex region that goes furthest in a given direction. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the plane the region is an intersection of half-planes, and the direction is a vector c. Part 23 builds the simplex method for thousands of dimensions; in two, Raimund Seidel's algorithm from 1991 fits in a dozen lines. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add the constraints one at a time, in random order, keeping the optimum of those seen so far. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the current optimum satisfies the new constraint, nothing changes. <bookmark mark='d'/> If it violates it, the new optimum must lie on the new constraint's line, and finding it there is a one-dimensional problem: intersect the line with the earlier constraints, an interval, and take the better end. Watch: of nine constraints, only three move the optimum.
f4a69ad1e9cf.zh: 线性规划求的是凸区域中沿给定方向走得最远的点。<bookmark mark='a'/>在平面上，区域是半平面的交，方向是一个向量 c。第23部分为成千上万个维度构造单纯形法；在二维中，Raimund Seidel 1991年的算法只要十几行。<bookmark mark='b'/>按随机顺序一次加一个约束，保存目前所见约束的最优解。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果当前最优解满足新约束，什么都不变。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果违反了，新的最优解必定在新约束的直线上，在那里求它是一个一维问题：把这条直线与之前的约束相交，得到一个区间，取较好的一端。看：九个约束中，只有三个移动了最优解。

4641664e2f92.en: How much does this cost? <bookmark mark='a'/> Backwards analysis once more. After i constraints, the optimum is a corner where two constraint lines meet. The i-th constraint, a random one of the i, moved the optimum only if it is one of those two. <bookmark mark='b'/> That happens with probability at most two over i, and then costs order i. Summed, the expected work is linear. <bookmark mark='c'/> We ran it on up to a hundred thousand random constraints. The optimum moved about as often as two times the harmonic number predicts, twenty-three times among a hundred thousand constraints, and the total one-dimensional work came to fewer than three steps per constraint, falling as n grew. In d dimensions the same algorithm takes d factorial times n, and Nimrod Megiddo showed in 1984 that linear time is possible deterministically for any fixed dimension.
4641664e2f92.zh: 这要花多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>又是反向分析。加入 i 个约束之后，最优解是两条约束线相交的角点。第 i 个约束是这 i 个中随机的一个，只有当它是那两个之一时，最优解才会移动。<bookmark mark='b'/>这种情况的概率至多是二除以 i，代价是 i 的阶。求和，期望工作量是线性的。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在多达十万个随机约束上运行它。最优解移动的次数大约正如两倍调和数所预测，十万个约束中移动了二十三次，一维工作的总量每个约束不到三步，且随 n 增大而减少。在 d 维中同样的算法需要 d 的阶乘乘以 n，而 Nimrod Megiddo 在1984年证明，对任何固定维度都可以确定性地做到线性时间。

dfe93fc8aa93.en: The same trick solves a different problem: the smallest circle that encloses a set of points, where to put one radio mast to cover a set of houses. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add the points in random order. While a new point is inside the current circle, nothing changes. When it falls outside, the new smallest circle must pass through it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Finding that circle is the same problem one level down, with one point fixed on the boundary, and then two. <bookmark mark='c'/> A circle is fixed by at most three points, so backwards analysis says the i-th point breaks it with probability at most three over i. <bookmark mark='d'/> We counted: a hundred thousand points rebuilt the circle only twenty-nine times, within three times the natural logarithm, and the whole computation took half a second in Python. <bookmark mark='e'/> Emo Welzl's algorithm runs in expected linear time, and Megiddo had found a deterministic one in 1983.
dfe93fc8aa93.zh: 同样的技巧解决另一个问题：包含一组点的最小圆，即在哪里立一根天线能覆盖一批房屋。<bookmark mark='a'/>按随机顺序加入点。新点在当前圆内时，什么都不变；它落在圆外时，新的最小圆必定经过它。<bookmark mark='b'/>求那个圆是低一层的同一个问题，边界上固定一个点，然后两个。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个圆至多由三个点决定，所以反向分析表明第 i 个点打破它的概率至多是三除以 i，期望重建次数至多是调和数的三倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们数了：十万个点只重建了二十九次圆，接近这个平均值，整个计算在 Python 中用了半秒。<bookmark mark='e'/>Emo Welzl 的算法期望线性时间，而 Megiddo 在1983年已找到一个确定性的。

75f0108bccba.en: A database of shops, each with a position, is asked for every shop in a rectangle on the map. Checking every shop is linear; we want the answer in time close to its size. <bookmark mark='a'/> Jon Bentley's kd-tree, from 1975, splits the points at their median x, then each half at its median y, then each quarter at its median x again, alternating, until every cell holds one point. <bookmark mark='b'/> It takes n log n to build and linear space. <bookmark mark='c'/> To answer a query, descend from the root into every cell that meets the rectangle, and report the points inside. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here the query visits forty-six of the hundred and nineteen nodes. <bookmark mark='e'/> Why is that cheap? A vertical line crosses only the cells along one path in every two levels, about the square root of n of them, so the query costs root n for the rectangle's boundary plus the k points reported. <bookmark mark='f'/> Bentley invented it as an undergraduate at Stanford.
75f0108bccba.zh: 一个商店数据库，每家商店有一个位置，被要求找出地图上一个矩形内的所有商店。检查每家商店是线性的；我们希望答案所需时间接近答案本身的大小。<bookmark mark='a'/>Jon Bentley 1975年的 kd 树先在 x 的中位数处分开点集，再在每一半的 y 中位数处分开，再在每个四分之一的 x 中位数处分开，交替进行，直到每个格子只含一个点。<bookmark mark='b'/>构造需要 n log n，空间是线性的。<bookmark mark='c'/>回答查询时，从根往下进入每个与矩形相交的格子，报告其中的点。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里查询访问了一百一十九个节点中的四十六个。<bookmark mark='e'/>为什么这么便宜？一条竖直线每两层只穿过一条路径上的格子，大约 n 的平方根个，所以查询代价是矩形边界的根号 n 加上报告的 k 个点。<bookmark mark='f'/>Bentley 是在斯坦福读本科时发明它的。

a2e013f81d47.en: We built kd-trees of up to three hundred thousand random points and asked forty small square queries of each. <bookmark mark='a'/> The visits stay below root n plus k: about three hundred and thirty nodes for three hundred thousand points, where a scan would look at all of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> The square root is the price of linear space, and it gets worse with dimension: in d dimensions a kd-tree query costs n to the one minus one over d, a warning for chapter twelve.
a2e013f81d47.zh: 我们为多达三十万个随机点构造了 kd 树，对每棵树各做了四十次小正方形查询。<bookmark mark='a'/>访问数一直低于根号 n 加 k：三十万个点大约访问三百三十个节点，而扫描要看全部的点。<bookmark mark='b'/>平方根是线性空间的代价，而且随维度变差：在 d 维中 kd 树的查询代价是 n 的一减 d 分之一次方，这是给第十二章的一个警告。

4f71b80d6c24.en: If we can afford more space, queries get faster. <bookmark mark='a'/> A range tree is a balanced tree on x in which every node also keeps its points sorted by y. <bookmark mark='b'/> It uses n log n space and answers in log squared n plus k. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bernard Chazelle and Leonidas Guibas removed a log with fractional cascading: each sorted list keeps pointers into its children's lists, so a single binary search at the root serves the whole path down. <bookmark mark='d'/> Interval trees and segment trees answer the other common question, which stored intervals contain a given point. <bookmark mark='e'/> Databases use R-trees, which pack nearby rectangles into the pages of a B-tree; they sit under PostGIS, SQLite's spatial index and most map servers.
4f71b80d6c24.zh: 如果负担得起更多空间，查询就更快。<bookmark mark='a'/>范围树是一棵按 x 建的平衡树，每个节点还保存按 y 排序的点。<bookmark mark='b'/>它使用 n log n 的空间，回答用 log 平方 n 加 k。<bookmark mark='c'/>Bernard Chazelle 与 Leonidas Guibas 用分散层叠去掉了一个 log：每个有序列表保存指向其孩子列表的指针，于是根处的一次二分查找就能服务一整条向下的路径。<bookmark mark='d'/>区间树和线段树回答另一个常见问题：哪些存储的区间包含给定的点。<bookmark mark='e'/>数据库使用 R 树，它把相邻的矩形装进 B 树的页中；PostGIS、SQLite 的空间索引和大多数地图服务器的底层都是它。

9da28ff9f11b.en: Your phone knows its coordinates; which country, which county, which time zone is it in? <bookmark mark='a'/> A map is a subdivision of the plane by n segments, and point location asks which face holds a query point. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first fast answer, by David Dobkin and Richard Lipton in 1976, draws a vertical line through every endpoint. Inside one slab no two segments cross, so they are sorted from bottom to top. <bookmark mark='c'/> A query is two binary searches: one for the slab, one for the segment just below the point. That is log n time. <bookmark mark='d'/> The trouble is space: a long segment crosses many slabs, and can be stored in every one, n squared in the worst case.
9da28ff9f11b.zh: 你的手机知道它的坐标；它在哪个国家、哪个县、哪个时区？<bookmark mark='a'/>地图是由 n 条线段对平面的划分，点定位问的是哪个面包含查询点。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一个快速的答案来自1976年的 David Dobkin 与 Richard Lipton：过每个端点画一条竖直线。在一个竖条内没有两条线段相交，所以它们从下到上是有序的。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次查询是两次二分查找：一次找竖条，一次找点正下方的线段。这是 log n 时间。<bookmark mark='d'/>麻烦在于空间：一条长线段穿过许多竖条，可能在每一个里都要存一次，最坏情况下是 n 的平方。

a2a2ee100a45.en: The fix is to stop the walls early. <bookmark mark='a'/> From each endpoint, draw a wall up and a wall down, but only as far as the nearest segment. The plane falls into trapezoids. <bookmark mark='b'/> These seven segments make twenty-two trapezoids, <bookmark mark='c'/> and that is no accident: every trapezoid's left side is fixed by one endpoint; a left endpoint can play that part for at most two trapezoids, and a right endpoint for one, so there are never more than three n plus one. On twenty random maps of five, twenty and eighty segments, every one hit the bound exactly. <bookmark mark='d'/> To query it fast, insert the segments in random order and keep a record of how each trapezoid was split, a search structure shaped like a directed acyclic graph. <bookmark mark='e'/> Ketan Mulmuley and Raimund Seidel showed that it has expected linear size and answers in logarithmic time. <bookmark mark='f'/> The proof is backwards analysis, a third time. David Kirkpatrick had reached the same bounds deterministically in 1983, with a hierarchy of ever coarser triangulations.
a2a2ee100a45.zh: 解决办法是让墙早点停下。<bookmark mark='a'/>从每个端点向上、向下各画一堵墙，但只延伸到最近的线段。平面就分成了梯形。<bookmark mark='b'/>这七条线段构成二十二个梯形，<bookmark mark='c'/>这不是巧合：每个梯形的左边由一个端点决定；一个左端点至多为两个梯形扮演这个角色，一个右端点为一个，所以梯形永远不超过三 n 加一个。在五条、二十条和八十条线段的各二十张随机地图上，每一张都恰好达到这个界。<bookmark mark='d'/>为了快速查询，按随机顺序插入线段，并记录每个梯形是怎样被分开的，这是一个形如有向无环图的搜索结构。<bookmark mark='e'/>Ketan Mulmuley 和 Raimund Seidel 证明它的期望大小是线性的，查询是对数时间。<bookmark mark='f'/>证明是第三次用到反向分析。David Kirkpatrick 在1983年用一层层越来越粗的三角剖分，确定性地达到了同样的界。

32bcc919622d.en: Everything so far lives in the plane, but the questions of chapters ten and eleven are asked of data with hundreds of dimensions: images, documents and the embeddings of the AI series. <bookmark mark='a'/> There, geometry behaves strangely. Take two thousand random points in a cube and measure their distances from a random query. In two dimensions the farthest point is a hundred times farther than the nearest; in a hundred dimensions, less than one and a half times; in a thousand, eleven percent. Almost every point is almost equally far away, and 'nearest' barely means anything. <bookmark mark='b'/> That ruins the kd-tree. Its pruning works only when the query's ball is small compared with the cells. For twenty thousand points, finding one nearest neighbour visits six hundredths of a percent of the nodes in two dimensions, half of them in twelve, and every single one in twenty-four: worse than a scan. <bookmark mark='c'/> Exact nearest neighbours in high dimensions seem to need either exponential space or nearly linear time, and the frontier chapter returns to that.
32bcc919622d.zh: 到目前为止的一切都在平面上，但第十章和第十一章的问题也会对几百维的数据提出：图像、文档，以及 AI 系列中的嵌入向量。<bookmark mark='a'/>在那里，几何表现得很奇怪。在立方体中取两千个随机点，测量它们到一个随机查询点的距离。在二维中，最远的点比最近的远一百倍；在一百维中，不到一点五倍；在一千维中，只远百分之十一。几乎每个点都几乎同样远，“最近”几乎失去了意义。<bookmark mark='b'/>这毁掉了 kd 树。它的剪枝只在查询球比格子小时才有效。对两万个点，找一个最近邻在二维中访问万分之六的节点，十二维中访问一半，二十四维中每一个都要访问：比扫描还糟。<bookmark mark='c'/>高维中精确的最近邻似乎要么需要指数级空间，要么需要接近线性的时间，前沿一章会回到这个问题。

125a9a578019.en: Two ideas rescue nearest neighbours by giving up exactness. Part 20's locality-sensitive hashing is one: hash so that near points tend to collide. The other, which dominates practice today, is a graph. <bookmark mark='a'/> Link each point to a few of its near neighbours, chosen to point in different directions. <bookmark mark='b'/> To answer a query, start anywhere and keep stepping to whichever neighbour is closer to the query, keeping a short list of the best seen. <bookmark mark='c'/> Yury Malkov and Dmitry Yashunin's hierarchical version adds sparser layers on top, like the express lanes of a skip list: a few long hops near the top, then a careful search at the bottom. <bookmark mark='d'/> We built one over twenty thousand points in sixteen dimensions, clustered around two hundred centres; it has four layers. <bookmark mark='e'/> There is no worst-case theorem for these graphs, but they are what vector databases run, behind retrieval for language models.
125a9a578019.zh: 有两个想法以放弃精确为代价挽救了最近邻。第20部分的局部敏感哈希是其一：让相近的点倾向于碰撞。另一个，也是今天实践中占主导的，是图。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个点连到它的几个近邻，选取时让它们指向不同的方向。<bookmark mark='b'/>回答查询时，从任意处出发，不断走向离查询点更近的那个邻居，同时保留一份所见最好者的短列表。<bookmark mark='c'/>Yury Malkov 与 Dmitry Yashunin 的分层版本在上面加了更稀疏的层，就像跳表的快车道：在顶部跳几次远的，再在底部仔细搜索。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们为十六维中的两万个点构造了一个，这些点聚集在两百个中心周围；它有四层。<bookmark mark='e'/>这些图没有最坏情况的定理，但向量数据库运行的正是它们，为语言模型的检索提供支持。

8eba552519e4.en: Here is what the layers and the choice of links buy, on a hundred queries. <bookmark mark='a'/> Brute force computes all twenty thousand distances for every query. <bookmark mark='b'/> A single-layer graph that links each point to its plain nearest neighbours does badly on clustered data: links stay inside clusters, and greedy searches get stuck in the wrong one: with a narrow beam it finds fewer than half of the true neighbours, and even its widest beam costs over six hundred computations. <bookmark mark='c'/> With HNSW's rule, keep a neighbour only if it is closer to the new point than to the neighbours already kept, so links fan out and bridge clusters, the layered graph finds ninety-nine point seven percent of the true ten nearest with under two hundred distance computations, a hundredth of brute force. <bookmark mark='d'/> Libraries like FAISS and pgvector run exactly this, under the retrieval systems that feed language models.
8eba552519e4.zh: 这是分层和链接的选择在一百个查询上带来的效果。<bookmark mark='a'/>暴力搜索对每个查询要计算全部两万个距离。<bookmark mark='b'/>只把每个点连到最近邻居的单层图在成簇的数据上表现很差：链接留在簇内，贪心搜索陷进错误的簇：用窄的束宽时它找到的真正近邻不到一半，即使最宽的束也要花六百多次计算。<bookmark mark='c'/>用 HNSW 的规则，只有当一个邻居离新点比离已保留的邻居都近时才保留它，于是链接向四面展开并跨越簇；分层图用不到两百次距离计算就找到了真正 10 个最近邻中的百分之九十九点七，是暴力搜索的百分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>FAISS 和 pgvector 这样的程序库运行的正是这个，它们在为语言模型提供数据的检索系统之下。

1558a4805410.en: Chapter thirteen. Duality and the ham sandwich.
1558a4805410.zh: 第13章。对偶与火腿三明治。

8b0ebcfc896b.en: Some of geometry's best tricks change what the objects are. <bookmark mark='a'/> Send the point a, b to the line y equals a x minus b. Each point on the left becomes a line on the right, in the same colour. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now take the line through two of the points: the white one. It becomes a single point, and that point is exactly where the two dual lines cross. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the map preserves above and below: a point above a line becomes a line above a point. So a question about points and the lines through them becomes a question about lines and their crossings, and sometimes the second is much easier to answer.
8b0ebcfc896b.zh: 几何中一些最好的技巧改变了对象本身。<bookmark mark='a'/>把点 a、b 映到直线 y 等于 a x 减 b。左边的每个点都变成右边一条同色的直线。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在取过其中两个点的直线：白色那条。它变成一个点，而那个点恰好就是两条对偶直线的交点。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个映射还保持上下关系：在直线上方的点变成在点上方的直线。所以关于点及过它们的直线的问题，变成了关于直线及其交点的问题，而后者有时容易回答得多。

7f33d36ca59e.en: Dual lines meet in arrangements. <bookmark mark='a'/> n lines in general position cut the plane into about n squared over two faces. <bookmark mark='b'/> The zone theorem says a new line passes through faces whose boundaries have only order n edges in all, so the whole arrangement can be built incrementally in n squared time. <bookmark mark='c'/> That answers questions like this: are any three of n points on one line? Dualize, and ask whether any three dual lines pass through one vertex of the arrangement. <bookmark mark='d'/> n squared, and nobody knows how to do it fundamentally faster; the frontier chapter explains why that is no accident. <bookmark mark='e'/> The same duality turns the hull of a set of points into an intersection of half-planes, and it is the reason the Voronoi diagram is an upper envelope of planes.
7f33d36ca59e.zh: 对偶直线相交构成排列。<bookmark mark='a'/>一般位置的 n 条直线把平面分成大约 n 平方除以二个面。<bookmark mark='b'/>区域定理说，一条新直线穿过的那些面的边界总共只有 n 阶条边，所以整个排列可以在 n 平方时间内增量构造。<bookmark mark='c'/>这能回答这样的问题：n 个点中有没有三点共线？做对偶，再问是否有三条对偶直线经过排列的同一个顶点。<bookmark mark='d'/>n 平方，而没有人知道怎样从根本上做得更快；前沿一章会解释这不是偶然。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的对偶把一组点的凸包变成半平面的交，这也是 Voronoi 图是平面的上包络的原因。

e2433917e0d0.en: One more theorem with a sandwich in its name. <bookmark mark='a'/> Scatter red points and blue points. Is there a single line that cuts both sets in half? <bookmark mark='b'/> Always. Arthur Stone and John Tukey proved in 1942 that in d dimensions one hyperplane halves any d sets: bread, ham and cheese in three. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here nine red and nine blue points, and a line with four of each on either side and one of each on it. <bookmark mark='d'/> We found it by trying lines through a red and a blue point; Lo, Matoušek and Steiger find it in linear time, by dualizing the points to lines and pruning. <bookmark mark='e'/> Halving cuts like this are how geometric divide-and-conquer splits its work evenly.
e2433917e0d0.zh: 再看一个名字里有三明治的定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>散布一些红点和蓝点。有没有一条直线能同时把两组都平分？<bookmark mark='b'/>总是有。Arthur Stone 与 John Tukey 在1942年证明，在 d 维中一个超平面可以同时平分任意 d 个集合：在三维中就是面包、火腿和奶酪。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里有九个红点和九个蓝点，一条直线两侧各有四个红点和四个蓝点，线上各一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们通过尝试过一个红点和一个蓝点的直线找到它；Lo、Matoušek 与 Steiger 把点对偶成直线并加以剪枝，在线性时间内找到它。<bookmark mark='e'/>这样的平分切割正是几何分治均匀分配工作的方式。

94736d673a8a.en: A robot must get from here to the star without touching the obstacles. Make it a triangle that can slide but not turn. <bookmark mark='a'/> The trick, due to Tomás Lozano-Pérez and Michael Wesley in 1979, is to change what moves. Slide the robot around an obstacle, touching it, and its reference corner traces a bigger shape: the obstacle grown by the robot, a Minkowski sum. <bookmark mark='b'/> Do that for every obstacle. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the robot is a single point, its reference corner, and it must avoid the grown obstacles. That is configuration space. <bookmark mark='d'/> A shortest path around polygons bends only at their corners, so join every pair of corners that can see each other: the visibility graph. <bookmark mark='e'/> Dijkstra's algorithm from Part 18 finds the shortest route through it, and the real triangle follows it, brushing the obstacles at every bend.
94736d673a8a.zh: 机器人必须从这里到达星形处而不碰到障碍物。让它是一个只能滑动、不能转动的三角形。<bookmark mark='a'/>Tomás Lozano-Pérez 与 Michael Wesley 在1979年的技巧是改变移动的对象。让机器人贴着一个障碍物滑一圈，它的参考角就描出一个更大的形状：被机器人扩大了的障碍物，一个 Minkowski 和。<bookmark mark='b'/>对每个障碍物都这样做。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在机器人是一个点，即它的参考角，必须避开扩大后的障碍物。这就是构形空间。<bookmark mark='d'/>绕多边形的最短路径只在它们的角上转弯，所以把每对彼此可见的角连起来：可见性图。<bookmark mark='e'/>第18部分的 Dijkstra 算法求出穿过它的最短路线，真正的三角形沿着它走，每次转弯都擦过障碍物。

48d8ecd6a4ca.en: The visibility graph needs the corners of every obstacle, and in higher dimensions there is no such thing to list. <bookmark mark='a'/> Steven LaValle's rapidly-exploring random tree needs only a collision test. Throw a random point into the space, find the nearest node of the tree, take a short step towards the random point, and keep the step if it hits nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> The tree spreads into the empty space, because big unexplored regions attract the most samples, and after a hundred and thirty-seven nodes it reaches the goal. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its path is not the shortest; the green one is. <bookmark mark='d'/> Over twenty runs every tree found a way, about thirty percent longer than the optimum. Later variants, like RRT star, keep rewiring the tree and converge to the shortest path. <bookmark mark='e'/> That trade, a little length for no geometry at all, is what makes sampling the standard in robotics.
48d8ecd6a4ca.zh: 可见性图需要每个障碍物的角，而在更高维中根本没有这样的东西可以列出。<bookmark mark='a'/>Steven LaValle 的快速探索随机树只需要一个碰撞测试。往空间里随机投一个点，找到树上最近的节点，朝那个随机点走一小步，如果没有碰到任何东西就保留这一步。<bookmark mark='b'/>树向空旷处蔓延，因为大片未探索的区域吸引最多的样本，长到一百三十七个节点时它到达了目标。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的路径不是最短的；绿色那条才是。<bookmark mark='d'/>二十次运行中每棵树都找到了路，平均比最优长约百分之三十。后来的变体如 RRT 星会不断重连这棵树，收敛到最短路径。<bookmark mark='e'/>用一点长度换来完全不需要几何，这个交易让采样成为机器人学的标准做法。

9bffddfecc69.en: Real robots turn. <bookmark mark='a'/> Rotation adds a dimension: the configuration space of a rigid body in the plane is three-dimensional, and an arm with seven joints lives in seven. <bookmark mark='b'/> John Reif showed in 1979 that the general piano mover's problem, many parts moving together, is PSPACE-hard. <bookmark mark='c'/> John Canny found an exact algorithm singly exponential in the dimension, which is about the best one can hope for. <bookmark mark='d'/> In practice, planners sample, with probabilistic roadmaps and random trees like the one we just grew, and they plan for factory arms and self-driving cars. <bookmark mark='e'/> The same primitives test collisions in games, build meshes for simulation, and organize scenes for ray tracing, which Part 51 builds.
9bffddfecc69.zh: 真实的机器人会转动。<bookmark mark='a'/>转动增加一个维度：平面上刚体的构形空间是三维的，而一条有七个关节的机械臂生活在七维中。<bookmark mark='b'/>John Reif 在1979年证明，一般的钢琴搬运工问题，即许多部件一起移动，是 PSPACE 难的。<bookmark mark='c'/>John Canny 找到了一个关于维度单指数的精确算法，这大约是所能期望的最好结果。<bookmark mark='d'/>实践中，规划器采用采样，用概率路线图和像我们刚刚生长的那种随机树，它们为工厂机械臂和自动驾驶汽车做规划。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的基本操作用于游戏中的碰撞检测、为模拟构造网格，以及为光线追踪组织场景，第51部分会构造它。

600aeb4204ce.en: Chapter fifteen. Frontier: exactness, three-sum, and nearest neighbours.
600aeb4204ce.zh: 第15章。前沿：精确性、3SUM 与最近邻。

627606afc0ee.en: The frontier has three fronts. The first is the one this part began with. <bookmark mark='a'/> Chee Yap's paradigm of exact geometric computation says: decide every predicate exactly, and the combinatorial structure, which points are on the hull, which triangles are Delaunay, will always be right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Exactness has a price. On nearly collinear points, our rational orientation test is about a hundred and twenty times slower than floating point. <bookmark mark='c'/> Adaptive filters pay it only where the answer is in doubt, which is how CGAL, LEDA and Shewchuk's Triangle mesh generator work. <bookmark mark='d'/> Inputs that really are degenerate, three points exactly on a line, can be handled by pretending the points were perturbed by infinitesimals, consistently. <bookmark mark='e'/> What remains hard is constructing new points. An intersection of two segments needs more bits than its endpoints, and intersecting the results again makes it worse, so long chains of constructions grow without bound. Snap rounding keeps them small at the cost of moving things slightly, and how to do that well in three dimensions is still open.
627606afc0ee.zh: 前沿有三条战线。第一条正是这一部分开始的地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>Chee Yap 的精确几何计算范式说：精确地判定每个谓词，组合结构，比如哪些点在凸包上、哪些三角形是 Delaunay 的，就总是对的。<bookmark mark='b'/>精确性是有代价的。在几乎共线的点上，我们的有理数方向测试比浮点数慢大约一百二十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>自适应过滤器只在答案可疑的地方付这个代价，CGAL、LEDA 和 Shewchuk 的 Triangle 网格生成器都是这样工作的。<bookmark mark='d'/>真正退化的输入，比如三个点恰好共线，可以假装这些点被无穷小量一致地扰动过来处理。<bookmark mark='e'/>仍然困难的是构造新点。两条线段的交点需要比端点更多的比特，再对结果求交就更糟，所以长串的构造会无限增长。吸附舍入以稍微移动物体为代价使它们保持很小，而在三维中怎样把这做好仍是开放问题。

5c742ccd78c3.en: The second front is a wall. <bookmark mark='a'/> The three-sum problem: given n numbers, do three of them add up to zero? Sorting and walking two pointers takes n squared. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now lift each number a to the point a, a cubed. Three numbers sum to zero exactly when their three points lie on one line; the algebra is a single factorization. <bookmark mark='c'/> We checked it on fourteen numbers: <bookmark mark='d'/> the two triples that sum to zero are exactly the two collinear triples. <bookmark mark='e'/> So collinearity is at least as hard as three-sum, and Anka Gajentaan and Mark Overmars showed in 1995 that a whole family of planar problems is: covering by strips, separating segments, motion planning among segments. <bookmark mark='f'/> The best three-sum algorithms beat n squared only by logarithmic factors, and the conjecture that nothing truly subquadratic exists has become a foundation of fine-grained complexity, which Part 27 builds.
5c742ccd78c3.zh: 第二条战线是一堵墙。<bookmark mark='a'/>3SUM 问题：给定 n 个数，是否有三个加起来等于零？排序后用两个指针走一遍需要 n 平方。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在把每个数 a 提升为点 a、a 的立方。三个数之和为零，恰好当它们的三个点在一条直线上；代数上只是一次因式分解。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在十四个数上核对了它：<bookmark mark='d'/>和为零的两个三元组恰好就是两个共线的三元组。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以共线性至少和 3SUM 一样难，而 Anka Gajentaan 与 Mark Overmars 在1995年证明了一整族平面问题都是如此：用带状区域覆盖、分隔线段、在线段之间规划运动。<bookmark mark='f'/>最好的 3SUM 算法只比 n 平方快对数因子，而不存在真正次平方算法的猜想，已成为细粒度复杂性的基础，第27部分会构造它。

5ed3b12b0abb.en: The third front is the one chapter twelve left open. <bookmark mark='a'/> For exact nearest neighbours in high dimensions, lower bounds in the cell-probe model suggest that no index can be both small and fast. <bookmark mark='b'/> For approximate ones there is a sharp theory. Locality-sensitive hashing answers a query for a c-approximate neighbour in time n to the one over c squared, and no hashing scheme that ignores the data can do better. <bookmark mark='c'/> Alexandr Andoni and Ilya Razenshteyn showed in 2015 that hashing adapted to the data does better, one over two c squared minus one, and that this too is optimal. <bookmark mark='d'/> Yet the graph indexes of chapter twelve beat every one of these methods in practice, with almost no theory behind them; Piotr Indyk and Haike Xu found inputs on which some popular graphs need linear time. <bookmark mark='e'/> Guarantees exist only for special data, of low doubling dimension, and special rules for building the graph.
5ed3b12b0abb.zh: 第三条战线是第十二章留下的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>对高维中的精确最近邻，单元探测模型中的下界表明，没有索引能既小又快。<bookmark mark='b'/>对近似最近邻有一套精确的理论。局部敏感哈希用 n 的一除以 c 平方次方的时间回答 c 近似最近邻查询，而任何不看数据的哈希方案都无法做得更好。<bookmark mark='c'/>Alexandr Andoni 与 Ilya Razenshteyn 在2015年证明，适应数据的哈希做得更好，二 c 平方减一分之一，而这也是最优的。<bookmark mark='d'/>然而第十二章的图索引在实践中胜过所有这些方法，背后几乎没有理论；Piotr Indyk 与 Haike Xu 找到了一些输入，让某些流行的图需要线性时间。<bookmark mark='e'/>只对特殊的数据，即倍增维数低的数据，以及特殊的建图规则，才有保证。

768c8f76f0b4.en: Here is where things stand. <bookmark mark='a'/> Can three-sum be solved in truly subquadratic time? <bookmark mark='b'/> Hopcroft's problem: given n points and n lines, does any point lie on any line? Jiří Matoušek's algorithm takes about n to the four thirds, and Jeff Erickson proved that bound optimal for a natural class of algorithms; for all algorithms, nobody knows. <bookmark mark='c'/> And why do navigable graphs work so well? A provable bound for HNSW-like graphs on realistic data, or a family of inputs that defeats them, is open. <bookmark mark='d'/> This part's research problem takes the third.
768c8f76f0b4.zh: 现状如下。<bookmark mark='a'/>3SUM 能在真正次平方的时间内解决吗？<bookmark mark='b'/>Hopcroft 问题：给定 n 个点和 n 条直线，是否有某个点在某条直线上？Jiří Matoušek 的算法大约需要 n 的三分之四次方，Jeff Erickson 证明这个界对一类自然的算法是最优的；对所有算法，没有人知道。<bookmark mark='c'/>可导航图为什么这么好用？为 HNSW 这类图在真实数据上证明一个界，或者找到一族能击败它们的输入，都还是开放问题。<bookmark mark='d'/>这一部分的研究题针对第三个问题。

e27ace358f4c.en: What we built in this part. An orientation test that is never wrong, at almost no cost. Five convex hull algorithms, and the reduction from sorting that bounds them all. The sweep line, and guards for an art gallery. Voronoi diagrams by Fortune's sweep, Delaunay triangulations by flips and by random insertion, and the paraboloid that makes them one thing. Backwards analysis, linear programming, kd-trees, point location, navigable graphs in high dimensions, and a robot that slides between obstacles.
e27ace358f4c.zh: 这一部分我们构造了：一个从不出错、几乎不花代价的方向测试。五个凸包算法，以及界住它们全部的、来自排序的归约。扫描线，以及美术馆的守卫。用 Fortune 扫描得到的 Voronoi 图，用翻转和随机插入得到的 Delaunay 三角剖分，以及把它们合而为一的抛物面。反向分析、线性规划、kd 树、点定位、高维中的可导航图，以及一个在障碍物间滑行的机器人。

897b4b436a7b.en: Where this comes back. Part 23 takes linear programming to many dimensions with the simplex method. Part 27 builds fine-grained complexity on three-sum. Part 47's search engine adds vector search over embeddings, with the graphs of chapter twelve, and Part 48 serves nearest-neighbour queries on maps. Part 51 draws triangles with the orientation test, which graphics calls an edge function, and traces rays through bounding-volume hierarchies. And Part 52 returns to floating point and computing with real numbers.
897b4b436a7b.zh: 它们会在哪里再出现。第23部分用单纯形法把线性规划带到多维。第27部分在 3SUM 之上构造细粒度复杂性。第47部分的搜索引擎加入嵌入向量上的向量搜索，用的是第十二章的图；第48部分在地图上提供最近邻查询。第51部分用方向测试绘制三角形，图形学称之为边函数，并在包围体层次结构中追踪光线。第52部分回到浮点数和实数计算。

8c43238e0f6f.en: In practice. Geographic systems like PostGIS and Google's S2 library run on exact predicates, R-trees and polygon overlay. CGAL and Shewchuk's Triangle build Delaunay meshes for simulation. Every graphics card rasterizes with orientation tests, and every game tests collisions. Robot planners search configuration spaces, and every vector database searches a navigable graph.
8c43238e0f6f.zh: 在实践中。PostGIS 和 Google 的 S2 库这样的地理系统运行在精确谓词、R 树和多边形叠加之上。CGAL 和 Shewchuk 的 Triangle 为模拟构造 Delaunay 网格。每块显卡都用方向测试做光栅化，每个游戏都要检测碰撞。机器人规划器搜索构形空间，而每个向量数据库都在搜索一张可导航图。

e91c4ec3cd71.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: the orientation test and the monotone chain in the Pebble language, run on the emulator. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
e91c4ec3cd71.zh: 六道题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一题上暂停。第五题是构造题：用 Pebble 语言写方向测试和单调链，在模拟器上运行。最后一题标有星号，是研究题：它的答案未知，笔记里说明了从哪里入手。

6039d15ffd5b.en: Next time, optimization. Many problems are a choice of the best point of a polytope. The simplex method walks the polytope's edges; duality certifies the answer from the other side. When integrality makes a problem hard, relaxations and random hyperplanes still get provably close, and online, without seeing the future, you can still be competitive. Part 23, Optimization.
6039d15ffd5b.zh: 下一次，优化。许多问题是在一个多面体中选出最好的点。单纯形法沿多面体的棱行走；对偶从另一侧证明答案。当整数性让问题变难时，松弛和随机超平面仍能可证明地逼近，而在线情形下，即使看不到未来，你仍然可以有竞争力。第23部分，优化。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书籍和论文显示在屏幕上，也列在笔记里。感谢观看。
